title: First Touch SDK Labs and Sample Accelerator Playbook
content:
Purpose and audience
--------------------
This is a lightweight, pragmatic playbook for 'first touch' experiences: the first 30–90 minutes a new integrator (internal engineer, customer engineer, or partner) spends with Redwood SDKs and sample apps. Audience: devs who want a runnable example fast and a checklist to reach a minimal, instrumented demo.

Why this exists
---------------
- We need a minimal, repeatable path that reduces friction to a working request and measurable telemetry within the first hour.
- Current quickstarts are either too long (full app walkthroughs) or too shallow (API call only). This sits between: runnable sample app + telemetry + troubleshooting notes.

Non-goals
--------
- Not a comprehensive API reference.
- Not replacing longer codelabs or in-person workshops.

Quick summary (30-minute path)
----------------------------
1) Prep (3 min): create free account or use sandbox token (link in README).
2) Clone tiny-sample-app repo, checkout 'first-touch' branch.
3) Install deps (npm/pip) and run local dev server.
4) Replace SAMPLE_KEY with token, run a single generation + streaming demo.
5) Open telemetry dashboard (devexp shortcut) to confirm request traces, latency, and token counts.
6) Triage checklist if it fails.

Files included in the kit
------------------------
- README-first-touch.md (single-page quickstart)
- tiny-sample-app/ (Node + Python minimal server with 2 routes)
- sample-prompts/ (3 prompts that show latency/cost tradeoffs)
- telemetry-mock/ (dev-only telemetry setup & dashboard link)
- smoke-tests/ (1-file scripts to run CI smoke)

Checklist for the leader running the lab (internal AE / SE)
---------------------------------------------------------
- [ ] Verify sandbox token is valid and scoped for 'generation' and 'embeddings'.
- [ ] Confirm local env (node >=18 or python 3.10).
- [ ] Have the short README printed or in a single tab for attendees.
- [ ] Start the telemetry dashboard and pre-filter by sandbox token.
- [ ] Start a screen-share and a shared slack channel for questions.

Detailed 60–90 minute lab flow (with timings)
--------------------------------------------
0–5 min: Orientation
- Quick context (what Redwood SDKs solve, what we'll see).
- Show the telemetry dashboard briefly so participants know what to expect.

5–20 min: Hands-on clone + run
- git clone .../tiny-sample-app.git
- npm install (or pip install -r requirements.txt)
- copy SAMPLE_KEY into .env
- npm run dev (or python -m tiny_server)
- Confirm the web page loads and a sample response is produced.

20–35 min: Instrumentation
- Walk through the tiny telemetry integration (2 hooks): request_id + token_metering.
- Run a couple of varying-length prompts from sample-prompts and watch token counts and latency in the dashboard.

35–50 min: Failure modes & recovery
- Simulate network failure: set SDK_BASE to unreachable and show fallback behaviour.
- Rotate token to invalid and show error message and suggested recovery steps.
- Show how to toggle batching / streaming in the sample app and the effect on latency and cost.

50–75 min: Customization sprint
- Add a second route to the sample app that calls the embeddings endpoint.
- Demonstrate how to add simple prompt templates and preserve telemetry labels.

75–90 min: Wrap up & next steps
- Share checklist to convert this sample into a PoC (security, rate limiting, rollout plan).
- Point to longer workshops, internal demo kit, and where to request Dedicated trials.

Troubleshooting quick hits
-------------------------
- 401 / "invalid key": check token prefix, ensure env var loaded.
- 502 / timeout: increase request timeout and try smaller prompt to see partial success.
- No telemetry visible: ensure the sample app sends the telemetry-api-key and the DevExp dashboard is filtered to the right token.
- Streaming hangs: confirm SSE support in the browser and proxy config (corporate proxies often break chunked responses).

Success metrics to capture after a session
----------------------------------------
- % of participants who get a first response within 15 minutes.
- Time to first telemetry trace (minutes).
- Number of labs that convert to a follow-up SE engagement.
- Feedback NPS on clarity and friction (simple 3-question form linked at end).

Guidance for embedding into other onramps
----------------------------------------
- Pair the 30-min path with a short video (3–4 minutes) that demonstrates the run and telemetry check.
- Add single-command installs: one-liners for brew, choco, apt (where possible).
- Provide a separate 'air-gap' checklist for customers on private deployments (what to pre-install, how to point SDKs at private endpoints).

Notes to authors / TODOs
-----------------------
- [ ] Replace sandbox links with canonical shortlinks (infra ticket to create).
- [ ] Add Windows-specific command snippets and CI smoke for Windows runners.
- [ ] Add localized README translations (es, fr) for partners in EU/APAC.
- [ ] Record short walkthrough video and attach to README.

Owner handoff instructions
-------------------------
If this playbook is adopted by Solutions or SEs, handoff list:
- Update the sandbox tokens monthly (owner: Aisha Romero).
- Keep the sample-prompts curated (owner: Jonah Li).
- Maintain the telemetry dashboard filter (owner: Priya Menon).

Appendix: small snippets (copy-paste)
----------------------------------
1) Minimal curl generation example
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SAMPLE_KEY"
  -H "Content-Type: application/json"
  -d '{"model":"redwood-alpha-1","input":"Write haiku about CI pipelines"}'

2) Node fetch example (2 lines)
await fetch('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate', { headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${SAMPLE_KEY}` }, method: 'POST', body: JSON.stringify({ model: 'redwood-alpha-1', input: 'Short summary of meeting' }) })

3) One-line CI smoke test (bash)
SAMPLE_KEY=xxx && curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $SAMPLE_KEY" -d '{"model":"redwood-alpha-1","input":"smoke"}'

Feedback & contact
------------------
Ping #devexp-playbooks on Slack for quick triage. For formal changes, open JIRA DEVEXP-482 and link PR to GH redwood/devexp/sdk-samples#108.

---
Small, modular, and instrumented is the design principle here. This doc should live alongside longer codelabs but be the fastest possible route to a measurable, running demo.
